teachingPrinciples: Keep each lesson between 15 and 20 minutes and finish with a strict result block.
Focus on practical life and immigration-relevant communication topics.
Correct mistakes immediately, kindly, and with one concise explanation.
Rotate exercises to combine recall, guided production, and free production.
Always end with a mini recap and next-focus hints before the JSON result.

modules.title: Foundations of Connection: Love, Valentine's Day, and warm introductions
lessonObjectives: Introduce yourself warmly in a romantic or friendly Valentine's context.
Use present tense forms of sein and haben to express feelings and preferences.
Build simple sentences about affection, compliments, invitations, and plans.
exercisePatterns: Fill in missing verb forms with romantic mini-dialogues.
Choose correct article and adjective in compliment sentences.
Answer invitation and date-planning prompts with new vocabulary.
funBreakIdeas: Word of the day tied to love and relationships.
completionChecks: Learner can produce five correct affection and invitation sentences.
Learner can ask and answer three Valentine's themed personal questions.

modules.title: Daily life: shopping, schedules, and local services
lessonObjectives: Handle common supermarket and appointment conversations.
Use modal verbs in short requests.

grammarTargets.name: Sentence connectors und/aber
grammarTargets.example: Ich komme, aber ich bin spat.

grammarTargets.name: Comparative forms
grammarTargets.example: Der Bus ist schneller als der Zug.

exercisePatterns: Build request sentences with modal verbs.
Correct article and case in product lists.
funBreakIdeas: Tip of the day about common checkout phrases.
Short tongue twister with supermarket words.
completionChecks: Learner can ask for products and prices naturally.
Learner can use mussen and konnen in five examples.

modules.title: Mobility and travel: appointments, vacation, and city life
lessonObjectives: Manage travel and city navigation conversations.
Use separable verbs in common mobility contexts.
Describe past experiences with Perfekt basics.

grammarTargets.name: Two-way prepositions basics
grammarTargets.example: Ich stelle die Tasche auf den Tisch.

grammarTargets.name: Subordinate clauses basics
grammarTargets.example: Ich bleibe hier, weil es regnet.

grammarTargets.name: Reflexive verbs intro
grammarTargets.example: Ich erinnere mich an den Termin.

grammarTargets.name: weil vs denn
grammarTargets.example: Ich gehe zu Fuss, denn der Bus kommt nicht.

completionChecks: Learner can ask for routes and schedules.
Learner can report three past actions in Perfekt.

modules.title: Work and social life: office routines and relationships
lessonObjectives: Discuss office routines and social plans.
Use subordinate clauses with weil and dass.
Practice reflexive verbs in daily contexts.

grammarTargets.name: Subordinate clauses with weil/dass
grammarTargets.example: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.

grammarTargets.name: Relative clauses intro
grammarTargets.example: Das ist der Kollege, der mir hilft.

grammarTargets.name: Genitive basics
grammarTargets.example: Das ist das Auto meines Nachbarn.

grammarTargets.name: Reported requests
grammarTargets.example: Sie sagt, ich soll morgen kommen.

exercisePatterns: Answer scenario questions about office and relationships.
funBreakIdeas: Light joke related to office communication.
completionChecks: Learner can justify choices using weil.

modules.title: Independence: narratives, opinions, and practical bureaucracy
lessonObjectives: Express and defend opinions in everyday topics.
Prepare for administrative and job-related interactions.

grammarTargets.name: Advanced relative clauses

grammarTargets.name: Prepositional verbs
grammarTargets.example: Ich bereite mich auf das Gespraech vor.
